todos.long_description: 🎯 **Objective:** Resolve the type check error "Type of close is unknown" in test_spell.py line 58nn📋 **Acceptance Criteria:**n- Identify why the close() method type is unknown to the type checkern- Fix the type annotation or import issue causing the errorn- Ensure the type checker recognizes the close() method properlyn- Verify the fix resolves the warning without breaking functionalitynn🚫 **Scope Boundaries:**n- **Included:** Type annotation fixes, import corrections, method signature updatesn- **Excluded:** Changes to the actual close() method implementation, unrelated type fixesn- **Clarification Required:** None - scope is clearnn🔧 **Technical Requirements:**n- Use proper type annotations for the spell objectn- Ensure type checker can resolve the close() method signaturen- Maintain compatibility with existing test functionalitynn📁 **Files/Components:**n- Update: [tests/test_spell.py] (fix type annotation for spell object)n- Investigate: [sorcererdb/spell.py] (check close method definition)nn🧪 **Testing Requirements:**n- Run type checker to verify error is resolvedn- Ensure tests still pass after type fixn- Validate no new type errors are introducednn⚠️ **Edge Cases:**n- Handle case where spell object might be Nonen- Consider inheritance/interface patterns if applicablen- Ensure fix works across different Python versionsnn📚 **Dependencies:** None

comments.content: **MANDATORY RESEARCH COMPLETED** ✅nn**Local Codebase Analysis:**nnI examined the type checking error in `tests/test_spell.py:58` where `spell.close()` is flagged as having an unknown type. Here's what I found:nn1. **Spell Class Definition** (`sorcererdb/spell.py:7`):n```pythonnclass Spell:n    def __init__(self, conn):n        self.conn     = connn        self.cursor   = Nonen        self.query    = Nonen        self.bindings = Nonen```nnThe `close()` method is defined at line 75:n```pythonndef close(self):n    self.cursor.close()n    self.cursor = Nonen    logger.debug(f"[Spell] Cursor closed")n```nn2. **Type Checking Configuration** (`pyrightconfig.json`):n- `typeCheckingMode`: "strict"n- `reportUnknownMemberType`: "warning"n- `pythonVersion`: "3.12"nn3. **Import Pattern** (`tests/test_spell.py:5`):n```pythonnfrom sorcererdb import SorcererDB, DBConfig, Spelln```nnThe Spell class is properly imported and the `close()` method exists, but the type checker can't infer the return type.nn**Internet Research (2025):**nn🔗 **[Pyright Type Checking Documentation](https://github.com/microsoft/pyright/blob/main/docs/configuration.md)**n- **Found via web search:** Official Pyright configuration and type checking documentationn- **Key Insights:** The `reportUnknownMemberType` setting controls warnings when member types cannot be determinedn- **Applicable to Task:** This explains why we're seeing the warning and how to configure itn- **Code Examples:** Configuration options for controlling type checking strictnessnn🔗 **[Python Type Annotations Best Practices](https://mypy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/cheat_sheet_py3.html)**n- **Found via web search:** Comprehensive guide to Python type annotationsn- **Key Insights:** Methods should have explicit return type annotations, especially in strict moden- **Applicable to Task:** The `close()` method needs a return type annotationn- **Code Examples:** `def close(self) -> None:` is the correct annotation for methods that don't return valuesnn🔗 **[Python Type Stubs and Annotations](https://peps.python.org/pep-484/)**n- **Found via web search:** PEP 484 specification for type hintsn- **Key Insights:** Type annotations help static analyzers understand method signaturesn- **Applicable to Task:** Adding `-> None` to the `close()` method will resolve the type checker warningn- **Code Examples:** Function annotations syntax and best practicesnn**Library Assessment:**n- **Current Version:** Pyright 1.1.403+ (from pyproject.toml)n- **Security Status:** Up-to-date and well-maintainedn- **Compatibility:** Works with Python 3.10+ as specified in project requirementsnn**Synthesis & Recommendation:**nnThe type check error occurs because the `close()` method in the Spell class lacks a return type annotation. In strict type checking mode, Pyright requires explicit type annotations for all methods. The fix is simple: add `-> None` to the method signature since `close()` doesn't return a value.nn**Recommended Solution:**n```pythonndef close(self) -> None:n    self.cursor.close()n    self.cursor = Nonen    logger.debug(f"[Spell] Cursor closed")n```nnThis will resolve the `reportUnknownMemberType` warning while maintaining the existing functionality.
